findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh the cache status shown in the dropdown
findings.body: The dropdown takes cacheUpdatedAt from the viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars query, but the deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. It never invalidates connectedCalendars. After a successful deletion, the 'Cache Status' entry and 'Delete cached data' item keep showing the old timestamp until something else refetches. Some callers do not pass onSuccess at all. The disconnect mutation in the same component invalidates connectedCalendars in onSettled, so the two mutations are inconsistent. Invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars after the cache delete as well.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted as en-US, ignoring the user's locale
findings.body: The timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) even though the surrounding label is translated through t() and useLocale() is already in scope. Non-English users see an English date format inside a localized sentence. Format with the user's locale instead.

findings.title: Empty fixed-width actions container is now rendered for cards with no actions
findings.body: The actions prop is now an always-truthy <div className="flex w-32 justify-end"> wrapping CredentialActionsDropdown. CredentialActionsDropdown returns null for delegation-owned credentials when disconnect is not allowed, and for non-Google credentials with no disconnect permission. Before this change, the old conditional expression evaluated to falsy in those cases, so no actions block was rendered. Now every such card reserves an empty 8rem-wide slot, which is a visible layout change. The same applies to the Alert branch at line 123. Only render the wrapper when the dropdown will render, or move the wrapper inside the dropdown.

findings.title: Legacy CalendarCache rows are backfilled with deploy time, so 'Last updated' is wrong
findings.body: Adding the column with DEFAULT NOW() sets updatedAt to the migration time for every existing CalendarCache row. The new status UI reads MAX(updatedAt) per credential and shows it as the last update time. For any cache entry not refreshed since deployment, the displayed time is the deploy time, not the real last write. The upsert sets expiresAt = write time + 30 days, so a better backfill is available: add the column nullable or with a default, then run UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - interval '30 days' for existing rows, and only then set NOT NULL.

findings.title: Every cache refresh now bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all of the credential's calendars
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now runs an unconditional updateMany on SelectedCalendar for the credential, across all event types, each time the cache is refreshed (webhook, unwatch repopulation, cron). The PR notes say no frontend reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt and that this write may be unnecessary. As written it adds a write per selected calendar on every refresh, and changes the meaning of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, with no consumer in this change. Remove it unless a real reader is added.

findings.title: Authorization and deletion path for deleteCache has no tests
findings.body: This new mutation has an access check (credential lookup by id AND userId, throwing otherwise) that guards a destructive delete. Nothing in the PR tests that another user's credentialId is rejected or that only the matching calendarCache rows are removed. The new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method and the enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler are also untested. The PR's checklist confirms only manual verification was done.

findings.title: Comment says CalendarCache has no updatedAt, which this PR now adds
findings.body: The TODO in getCachedAvailability says updatedAt 'doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table'. This PR adds that column, so the comment is now false and points readers at a non-existent gap. Update or remove it.

findings.title: Script uses BSD-only sed -i '' and a parent-relative .env path
findings.body: sed -i '' is macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU sed (Linux), '' is taken as the script and the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL update fails. ENV_FILE is also hard-coded to ../.env (line 5), relative to the current directory. Running the script from the repo root writes to a .env outside the repository. The script is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not mentioned in the PR description.

findings.title: Failure paths exit with status 0
findings.body: cleanup() ends with exit 0 unconditionally. It is also called from the rate-limit branch (line 49) and the 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' branch (line 58). Callers and CI cannot tell that the tunnel setup failed. Exit with a non-zero status on the failure paths.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx, which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The change from ts-node to npx tsx is unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not described in the PR. tsx is not listed in apps/web's dependencies or devDependencies, so npx has to resolve or download it at runtime. That can pick a different version or fail offline. Either declare tsx as a dev dependency or revert this change in this PR.
